headline: Independent groups that test AI models for safety are moving to the centre of the debate over whether leading AI companies can be trusted, CNBC reports.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a trend report on outside AI safety testing with one concrete company statement, but no new test result and the original could only be read through a relay.
importance_line: Anyone relying on AI companies' own safety claims gains a possible outside check, but questions remain over who funds the testing groups and how freely they can publish bad news, and this is a trend report, not a new finding.
source: CNBC, as relayed by Business Upturn
summary: CNBC reported on 11 Oct 2026, as relayed by Business Upturn, that independent AI safety testing groups are gaining prominence as Anthropic and OpenAI explore giving outside evaluators a bigger role, with open questions over who funds them, how freely they can publish bad news and how much access they get; Business Upturn names METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research), Apollo Research and Transluce among them. OpenAI said it is close to signing contracts with outside safety assessors and plans to share details within weeks.
notes: CNBC page blocked (HTTP 403); text read on Business Upturn, which cites CNBC. The CNBC link is the original; the group names and the OpenAI contract statement come through Business Upturn's relay.
